newsitem.title: USA: Florida consumer confidence rises in May - survey.
newsitem.headline: Florida consumer confidence rises in May - survey.

text.p: A record high stock market and media reports of a healthy economy spurred a two-point rise in the Florida consumer confidence index for May, University of Florida economists said Tuesday.
The index rose to 97, recovering the two points it lost between March and April.
"Consumers appear to be exuberant," said Chris McCarty, survey director for the university's Bureau of Economic and Business Research.
Disposable income has risen steadily since January and unemployment remains low, McCarty said.

Consumers are the most confident they have been in 20 months that now is a good time to buy expensive items such as appliances and refrigerators. That component of the index rose one point from April to 114 in May, the highest level since September 1995.
Despite high confidence and higher wages, there have been signs in the last two months that consumer spending nationally has started to wane, McCarty said.

"Auto sales, for example, fell slightly in April and March figures show a slight decrease in new and existing home sales," he said. "These declines are not reflected in the outlook of most consumers."

Employed Floridians gave similar reports of business activity as they did last month. For the second consecutive month, 52 percent of repondents said business was better than at the same time a year ago. The share of those who expected more employees to be hired at their workplace in the next six months increased to 39 pecent in May from 35 percent in April.
The monthly Florida survey was based on telephone interviews with 911 randomly selected adults and has an error margin of about three percent.
